# Fine-Tuning Model Architecture



Nicheformer's fine-tuning architecture adapts the pre-trained transformer backbone for supervised downstream tasks through a flexible modular design. This architecture enables efficient transfer learning across various spatial transcriptomics applications while preserving the rich biological representations learned during pretraining. The system provides two implementations—`NicheformerFineTune` (recommended) and `FineTuningModel` (alternative)—both built on PyTorch Lightning for streamlined training workflows.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L18-L92), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L15-L106)

## Architecture Overview

The fine-tuning architecture follows a modular design pattern where a frozen or partially-updated pre-trained backbone processes input sequences, extracting intermediate representations from specific transformer layers. These representations are combined using configurable aggregation functions and passed through task-specific prediction heads. The architecture supports multiple supervised tasks including regression for continuous niche composition values, classification for cell type labels, and density prediction for spatial analysis.

The key architectural components include: (1) the pre-trained Nicheformer backbone, (2) layer extraction mechanism that selects specific transformer encoder layers, (3) layer combination functions that aggregate multi-layer representations, (4) optional MLP extractor for additional transformation, and (5) task-specific linear prediction heads.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A[Input Sequence<br/>token indices] --> B[Token Embeddings]
    B --> C[Positional Encoding]
    C --> D[Transformer Encoder Layers]
    
    subgraph LayerExtraction["Layer Extraction"]
        D --> E[Layer 0]
        D --> F[Layer N-1]
        E --> G[Extract Selected Layers]
        F --> G
    end
    
    G --> H{Combination Function}
    H -->|mean| I[Mean Aggregation]
    H -->|sum| J[Sum Aggregation]
    H -->|concat| K[Concatenation]
    
    I --> L[Pooled Representations]
    J --> L
    K --> L
    
    L --> M{Extractor?}
    M -->|Yes| N[MLP Pooler Head<br/>Linear + Tanh]
    M -->|No| O[Direct Pass]
    
    N --> P[Linear Prediction Head]
    O --> P
    
    P --> Q{Task Type}
    Q -->|Regression| R[MSE Loss]
    Q -->|Classification| S[Cross-Entropy Loss]
    
    style D fill:#e1f5ff
    style G fill:#fff4e1
    style N fill:#ffe1e1
    style P fill:#e1ffe1
```

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L118-L174), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L107-L163)

## Core Components

### Pre-trained Backbone

The backbone is the pre-trained `Nicheformer` model that provides the foundational representations for fine-tuning. During initialization, the backbone's masking parameter (`masking_p`) is set to 0.0 since masked language modeling loss is no longer used during supervised fine-tuning. The backbone can be completely frozen or selectively updated based on the `freeze` parameter, enabling different transfer learning strategies. When `freeze=True`, all backbone parameters remain static, and only the task-specific prediction heads are trained. This approach is useful when the pre-trained representations are already well-suited for the downstream task or when working with limited training data.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L62-L67), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L60-L64)

### Layer Extraction Mechanism

The fine-tuning architecture extracts hidden representations from specific transformer encoder layers rather than using only the final output. This is controlled by the `extract_layers` parameter, which accepts a list of layer indices. For example, `extract_layers=[11]` extracts features only from the final transformer layer (layer 11 in a 12-layer model), while `extract_layers=[6, 11]` combines representations from both middle and final layers. This flexibility allows practitioners to leverage different levels of abstraction—earlier layers capture more local patterns while later layers encode higher-level biological concepts.

> [!TIP]
> The layer extraction mechanism enables you to experiment with different abstraction levels for your specific task. Earlier layers may be better for fine-grained spatial patterns, while later layers often capture more semantic biological relationships.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L130-L137), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L130-L138)

### Layer Combination Strategies

When multiple layers are extracted, their representations must be combined into a single feature vector. The `function_layers` parameter determines this aggregation strategy:

| Strategy | Description | Output Dimension | Use Case |
|----------|-------------|------------------|----------|
| `mean` | Element-wise average across layers | `dim_model` | Balanced integration of multi-scale features |
| `sum` | Element-wise sum across layers | `dim_model` | Emphasizes features present across multiple layers |
| `concat` | Concatenation along feature dimension | `dim_model × num_layers` | Preserves all layer-specific information |

The mean strategy is most commonly used as it provides smooth integration without drastically increasing dimensionality. Concatenation preserves the most information but increases computational cost and may require more training data to avoid overfitting.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L139-L145), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L140-L147)

## Task-Specific Prediction Heads

The architecture supports five supervised tasks, each with a specialized prediction head and loss function:

### Niche Regression

Predicts continuous values representing niche composition or cell-type proportions in the local microenvironment. Uses a linear head mapping from `dim_model` to `dim_prediction` dimensions (typically the number of cell types, e.g., 33), with MSE loss. Optionally supports distribution regression (`regress_distribution=True`) where predictions are normalized via softmax to sum to 1, representing probability distributions over niche compositions.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L93-L98), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L73-L76)

### Density Regression

Predicts a single scalar value representing cell density in the local microenvironment. Uses a linear head with one output dimension and MSE loss. This is useful for spatial analysis tasks where the number of surrounding cells is the target variable.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L99-L101), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L77-L79)

### Niche Classification

Performs multi-class classification to predict discrete niche or region labels. Uses a linear head mapping to `n_classes` dimensions with cross-entropy loss. The output shape is `(batch_size, n_classes)`, and the model predicts class indices directly.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L102-L104), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L80-L82)

### Binary Classification

Performs binary classification tasks, such as presence/absence of specific cell types or conditions. Uses a linear head with `dim_prediction` outputs and cross-entropy loss. Labels are automatically converted to binary (0 or 1) during training.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L105-L107), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L83-L85)

### Multi-class Classification

Handles multi-label classification scenarios where each sample can belong to multiple classes simultaneously. Uses a linear head with `dim_prediction × n_classes` outputs, allowing predictions for multiple labels per sample.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L108-L113), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L86-L88)

## Configuration Parameters

The fine-tuning architecture accepts numerous parameters that control its behavior:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `backbone` | `pl.LightningModule` | required | Pre-trained Nicheformer model |
| `supervised_task` | `str` | required | Task type: 'niche_regression', 'density_regression', 'niche_classification', etc. |
| `extract_layers` | `list[int]` | required | Indices of transformer layers to extract features from |
| `function_layers` | `str` | 'mean' | Method to combine extracted layers: 'mean', 'sum', 'concat' |
| `freeze` | `bool` | False | If True, freeze all backbone parameters |
| `reinit_layers` | `list[int]` \| `None` | None | Layers to reinitialize before training |
| `extractor` | `bool` | False | If True, add MLP pooler head before final linear layer |
| `lr` | `float` | 1e-4 | Learning rate |
| `warmup` | `int` | 10 | Number of warmup steps for LR scheduler |
| `max_epochs` | `int` | 50000 | Maximum training epochs |
| `dim_prediction` | `int` | 33 | Output dimension for regression tasks |
| `n_classes` | `int` | 60 | Number of classes for classification tasks |
| `regress_distribution` | `bool` | False | Normalize regression outputs to sum to 1 |
| `predict_density` | `bool` | False | Predict scalar cell density |
| `ignore_zeros` | `bool` | False | Ignore zero labels in classification |
| `without_context` | `bool` | True | Exclude context tokens from predictions |

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L19-L90), [src/nicheformer/config_files/_config_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/config_files/_config_fine_tune.py#L1-L21)

## Training Workflow

The training workflow follows a standard PyTorch Lightning pattern with task-specific loss computation and logging. During each training step, the model:

1. Receives a batch containing token indices, attention masks, and labels
2. Disables MLM masking by setting masking probability to 0.0
3. Processes the batch through the backbone to extract layer representations
4. Aggregates representations using the specified combination function
5. Applies optional MLP extractor and task-specific linear head
6. Computes task-specific loss (MSE for regression, Cross-entropy for classification)
7. Logs metrics to the training logger

The model implements `training_step`, `validation_step`, `test_step`, and `predict_step` methods following PyTorch Lightning conventions. The optimizer uses AdamW with the CosineWarmupScheduler, which gradually increases the learning rate during the warmup period then applies cosine annealing decay.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Batch Input<br/>tokens, attention_mask, label] --> B[Disable MLM Masking<br/>masking_p=0.0]
    B --> C[Forward Pass<br/>Backbone + Extraction]
    C --> D[Layer Combination<br/>mean/sum/concat]
    D --> E[Optional MLP Extractor<br/>if extractor=True]
    E --> F[Task-Specific Linear Head]
    F --> G{Task Type?}
    G -->|Regression| H[Compute MSE Loss]
    G -->|Classification| I[Compute Cross-Entropy Loss]
    H --> J[Backpropagation<br/>AdamW Optimizer]
    I --> J
    J --> K[Learning Rate Schedule<br/>Cosine Warmup]
    K --> L[Log Metrics]
    
    style C fill:#e1f5ff
    style F fill:#fff4e1
    style H fill:#ffe1e1
    style I fill:#ffe1e1
```

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L175-L218), [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L391-L406)

## Context Token Handling

The architecture provides flexibility in handling auxiliary context tokens through the `without_context` parameter. Context tokens are special tokens added to the input sequence that encode metadata about the sample (e.g., modality, species, assay). When `without_context=True` (default), the model excludes the first 3 tokens (typically auxiliary tokens) from pooling and prediction, using only the biological sequence tokens. When `without_context=False`, all tokens including context tokens are included in the pooled representation.

This design choice allows the model to either leverage contextual metadata in predictions or focus purely on the biological sequence content depending on the task requirements.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L161-L166), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L151-L156)

## Layer Reinitialization Strategy

The `reinit_layers` parameter enables selective reinitialization of transformer encoder layers before fine-tuning. When specified, the indicated layers have their weights reinitialized using the backbone's initialization function. This strategy is particularly useful when transferring to substantially different domains where some layers' pre-trained weights may be less relevant. For example, reinitializing the final few layers while keeping earlier layers frozen can help the model adapt to new downstream tasks while preserving lower-level feature extractors.

Sources: [src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L68-L72), [src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L66-L72)

## Next Steps

After understanding the fine-tuning architecture, you can explore specific task implementations:

- **[Classification Tasks with Fine-Tuning](19-classification-tasks-with-fine-tuning)**: Learn detailed strategies for classification tasks including multi-class and binary scenarios
- **[Regression Tasks and Density Prediction](20-regression-tasks-and-density-prediction)**: Dive deeper into regression tasks for niche composition and density prediction
- **[Layer Extraction and Reinitialization Strategies](21-layer-extraction-and-reinitialization-strategies)**: Understand best practices for selecting and configuring layer extraction strategies

For practical implementation examples, refer to the [downstream fine-tuning notebook](../notebooks/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.ipynb) which demonstrates end-to-end workflows for various tasks.


# Classification Tasks with Fine-Tuning



This guide explains how to fine-tune pre-trained Nicheformer models for classification tasks in spatial omics data. Fine-tuning adapts the foundation model's learned representations to predict discrete categorical labels such as cell types, tissue regions, or spatial niches.

## Classification Task Architecture

The fine-tuning architecture wraps a pre-trained Nicheformer backbone with a classification-specific prediction head. This design enables efficient transfer learning while preserving the powerful representations learned during pretraining across diverse spatial transcriptomics datasets.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L18-L93)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Pre-trained Nicheformer Backbone] --> B{Freeze Backbone?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Frozen Encoder]
    B -->|No| D[Trainable Encoder]
    
    C --> E[Multi-Layer Feature Extraction]
    D --> E
    
    E --> F{Combine Layers}
    F -->|Mean| G[Average Hidden States]
    F -->|Sum| H[Sum Hidden States]
    F -->|Concat| I[Concatenate Layers]
    
    G --> J{Use Extractor MLP?}
    H --> J
    I --> J
    
    J -->|Yes| K[MLP Pooler Head + Tanh]
    J -->|No| L[Direct Linear Head]
    
    K --> M[Linear Classification Head]
    L --> M
    
    M --> N[Class Logits]
    N --> O[CrossEntropyLoss]
    
    style A fill:#e3f2fd
    style M fill:#ffecb3
    style O fill:#ffcdd2
```

The architecture consists of five key components that transform pre-trained representations into classification predictions:

**Backbone Encoder**: The pre-trained Nicheformer transformer processes input token sequences through multi-layer attention mechanisms. You can optionally freeze these parameters to preserve pre-trained knowledge, or unfreeze them for full fine-tuning. When `freeze=True`, the backbone weights remain unchanged, and only the classification head is trained—this is particularly effective when the downstream task is similar to the pretraining domain.

**Layer Extraction Strategy**: Rather than using only the final transformer output, Nicheformer extracts features from intermediate layers specified by `extract_layers` (e.g., `[8, 10, 11]` for the top three layers). This captures multi-scale representations that improve classification performance. The extracted representations are then combined using one of three strategies: `"mean"` averages across layers, `"sum"` adds them together, or `"concat"` concatenates them to create higher-dimensional features.

> [!TIP]
> The choice of `extract_layers` significantly impacts performance. Deeper layers capture more task-specific features, while shallower layers preserve generalizable patterns. For complex classification tasks, extracting from multiple layers (e.g., `[8, 10, 11]`) and using mean pooling typically outperforms single-layer extraction.

**Optional Extractor MLP**: When `extractor=True`, an additional MLP layer (linear transformation + Tanh activation) is applied before the final classification head. This extractor follows the HuggingFace BERT-style pooler architecture and provides a learned transformation of the aggregated representations, which can improve performance on challenging classification tasks by adding non-linear capacity.

**Classification Head**: A linear layer maps the aggregated representations to class logits. For `niche_classification`, this produces `n_classes` logits—one per class. For `niche_binary_classification`, it produces `dim_prediction` logits (one per cell type), and for `niche_multiclass_classification`, it produces `dim_prediction * n_classes` logits for multi-label scenarios.

**Pooling Strategy**: The final token representations are pooled to create a fixed-size vector for each sample. The `"mean"` strategy averages all token representations (excluding auxiliary context tokens when `without_context=True`). The `"cls"` strategy uses a dedicated CLS token prepended to the sequence, similar to BERT. For spatial omics data, mean pooling is typically more effective as it captures the full context of the cellular neighborhood.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L93-L117), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L93-L140)

## Supported Classification Tasks

Nicheformer provides three distinct classification task types, each optimized for different downstream prediction scenarios in spatial omics analysis.

| Task Type | Prediction Shape | Loss Function | Use Case |
|-----------|------------------|---------------|----------|
| `niche_classification` | `(batch, n_classes)` | CrossEntropyLoss | Multi-class single-label classification (e.g., tissue region, spatial niche) |
| `niche_binary_classification` | `(batch, dim_prediction)` | CrossEntropyLoss | Binary classification per cell type (e.g., presence/absence) |
| `niche_multiclass_classification` | `(batch, n_classes, dim_prediction)` | CrossEntropyLoss | Multi-label classification (e.g., multiple marker expressions) |

**Niche Classification**: The most common task for spatial omics, this performs standard multi-class classification where each sample belongs to exactly one class. For example, classifying cells into spatial niche types or tissue regions. The model outputs `n_classes` logits, and the class with the highest score is selected as the prediction. This is ideal for categorical variables with mutually exclusive categories.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L106-L108)

**Niche Binary Classification**: This performs binary classification for each of `dim_prediction` categories (typically cell types). For each category, the model predicts whether it is present (1) or absent (0). This is useful for tasks like predicting which cell types are present in a cellular neighborhood, where multiple cell types can co-occur. Labels are automatically converted to binary format: `label = (label != 0).int()`.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L109-L111), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L180-L182)

**Niche Multi-class Classification**: This extends binary classification to multiple classes per category, enabling multi-label prediction scenarios. The output dimension is `dim_prediction * n_classes`, which is then reshaped to `(batch, n_classes, dim_prediction)` for loss computation. This allows predicting, for example, different expression levels or states for multiple cell types simultaneously.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L112-L115), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L133-L136)

## Configuration and Hyperparameters

Fine-tuning requires careful configuration of model architecture and training hyperparameters. The configuration system supports both Python dictionaries and YAML files, making it easy to experiment with different settings.

```python
config = {
    # Model paths and data
    'checkpoint_path': 'path/to/pretrained/model.ckpt',
    'data_path': 'path/to/data.h5ad',
    'technology_mean_path': 'path/to/technology_mean.npy',
    'output_path': 'path/to/predictions.h5ad',
    
    # Task specification
    'supervised_task': 'niche_classification',  # Task type
    'label': 'region',  # Column name to predict
    'organ': 'brain',  # Tissue type for logging
    
    # Model architecture
    'freeze': False,  # Freeze backbone weights
    'reinit_layers': None,  # Layers to reinitialize
    'extract_layers': [11],  # Which transformer layers to use
    'function_layers': 'mean',  # How to combine layers
    'extractor': False,  # Use MLP extractor
    'pool': 'mean',  # Pooling strategy
    'without_context': True,  # Exclude auxiliary tokens
    
    # Output dimensions
    'n_classes': 17,  # Number of classes for classification
    'dim_prediction': 1,  # Output dimension (task-dependent)
    
    # Training hyperparameters
    'batch_size': 32,
    'lr': 1e-4,
    'warmup': 10,
    'max_epochs': 100,
    'gradient_clip_val': 1.0,
    'accumulate_grad_batches': 10,
    'precision': 32,
    
    # Data loading
    'max_seq_len': 1500,
    'aux_tokens': 30,
    'chunk_size': 1000,
    'num_workers': 4,
}
```

Sources: [_config_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/config_files/_config_fine_tune.py#L1-L21), [downstream_fine_tune.ipynb](notebooks/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.ipynb#L38-L74)

### Key Configuration Parameters

The most critical parameters for successful fine-tuning are those controlling model architecture and training dynamics:

**Freeze Strategy**: Setting `freeze=True` is recommended when working with small datasets or when the downstream task closely matches the pretraining domain. This prevents catastrophic forgetting of the pre-trained representations and reduces the risk of overfitting. For larger datasets or significantly different tasks, setting `freeze=False` and using a lower learning rate (e.g., `1e-5`) allows the model to adapt more thoroughly to the new task.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L31-L32), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L47-L48)

**Layer Extraction**: The `extract_layers` parameter determines which transformer layers contribute to the final prediction. Common strategies include:
- `[11]` for using only the final layer (most task-specific features)
- `[8, 10, 11]` for multi-scale feature combination
- `[0, 5, 10, 11]` for capturing representations at all depth levels

The `function_layers` parameter controls how these extracted layers are combined, with `"mean"` being the most robust choice for most classification tasks.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L127-L143), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L107-L122)

**Learning Rate and Warmup**: Fine-tuning typically requires lower learning rates than pretraining. A common configuration is `lr=1e-4` with `warmup=10` steps, allowing the model to gradually increase the learning rate before decaying it following a cosine schedule. The warmup period helps stabilize training early in the fine-tuning process. Use the `LearningRateMonitor` callback to track learning rate changes throughout training.

Sources: [_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/_fine_tune.py#L37-L56), [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L391-L398)

> [!TIP]
> For classification tasks with class imbalance, consider using `ignore_zeros=True` to exclude zero-valued labels from loss computation. This prevents the model from being biased toward the majority class and can significantly improve performance on minority classes. The implementation automatically replaces zeros with `-100`, which PyTorch's CrossEntropyLoss ignores.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L35), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L195-L197)

## Training Workflow

The fine-tuning workflow follows a structured process from data loading through model training and prediction. This workflow is implemented in both script form (`_fine_tune.py`) and as an interactive notebook (`downstream_fine_tune.ipynb`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Load Pre-trained Checkpoint] --> B[Initialize FineTuningModel]
    B --> C[Configure Trainer]
    C --> D[Setup DataLoaders]
    D --> E[Training Loop]
    E --> F[Validation]
    F --> G[Test Evaluation]
    G --> H[Generate Predictions]
    H --> I[Save Results to AnnData]
    
    style A fill:#e3f2fd
    style E fill:#fff3e0
    style I fill:#e8f5e9
```

**Step 1: Model Loading**: Load the pre-trained Nicheformer model from a checkpoint path. The model architecture and hyperparameters are automatically restored, providing a solid foundation for fine-tuning.

```python
from nicheformer.models import Nicheformer, NicheformerFineTune

model = Nicheformer.load_from_checkpoint(
    checkpoint_path=config['checkpoint_path'],
    strict=False
)
```

Sources: [_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/_fine_tune.py#L13-L14), [downstream_fine_tune.ipynb](notebooks/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.ipynb#L165-L168)

**Step 2: Fine-Tuning Model Initialization**: Wrap the pre-trained backbone with the classification-specific components:

```python
fine_tune_model = NicheformerFineTune(
    backbone=model,
    supervised_task=config['supervised_task'],
    extract_layers=config['extract_layers'],
    function_layers=config['function_layers'],
    lr=config['lr'],
    warmup=config['warmup'],
    max_epochs=config['max_epochs'],
    dim_prediction=config['dim_prediction'],
    n_classes=config['n_classes'],
    freeze=config['freeze'],
    reinit_layers=config['reinit_layers'],
    extractor=config['extractor'],
    pool=config['pool'],
    organ=config['organ'],
    label=config['label'],
    without_context=True
)
```

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L19-L63), [downstream_fine_tune.ipynb](notebooks/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.ipynb#L170-L188)

**Step 3: Trainer Configuration**: Set up the PyTorch Lightning trainer with appropriate callbacks and settings:

```python
import pytorch_lightning as pl
from pytorch_lightning.callbacks import ModelCheckpoint, LearningRateMonitor

trainer = pl.Trainer(
    max_epochs=config['max_epochs'],
    accelerator='gpu',
    devices=1,
    precision=config.get('precision', 32),
    gradient_clip_val=config.get('gradient_clip_val', 1.0),
    accumulate_grad_batches=config.get('accumulate_grad_batches', 10),
    callbacks=[
        ModelCheckpoint(dirpath=config['output_dir'], every_n_train_steps=5000, save_top_k=-1),
        LearningRateMonitor(logging_interval='step')
    ]
)
```

Sources: [_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/_fine_tune.py#L37-L56), [downstream_fine_tune.ipynb](notebooks/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.ipynb#L190-L198)

**Step 4: Training**: Execute the training loop:

```python
trainer.fit(
    model=fine_tune_model,
    train_dataloaders=train_loader,
    val_dataloaders=val_loader
)
```

During training, the model logs both classification loss and accuracy metrics. The `training_step` method computes CrossEntropyLoss for classification tasks, with accuracy calculated as the proportion of correct predictions.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L175-L212), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L164-L213)

**Step 5: Prediction and Evaluation**: Generate predictions on the test set and store them in the AnnData object:

```python
# Test evaluation
test_results = trainer.test(fine_tune_model, dataloaders=test_loader)

# Get predictions
predictions = trainer.predict(fine_tune_model, dataloaders=test_loader)
class_logits = torch.cat([p[0] for p in predictions]).cpu().numpy()
class_probs = torch.cat([p[1] for p in predictions]).cpu().numpy()

# Store in AnnData
adata.obs.loc[test_mask, f"{prediction_key}_class"] = class_logits.argmax(axis=1)
adata.obs.loc[test_mask, f"{prediction_key}_class_probs"] = class_probs
adata.write_h5ad(config['output_path'])
```

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L305-L321), [downstream_fine_tune.ipynb](notebooks/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.ipynb#L227-L246)

## Advanced Features

**Layer Reinitialization**: When `reinit_layers` is specified, the selected transformer layers are reinitialized with random weights using a normal distribution (mean=0.0, std=0.02). This can be beneficial when the pre-trained features are not well-suited for the downstream task, allowing the model to learn task-specific representations at intermediate layers while preserving the general knowledge in the remaining layers.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L33-L37), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L50-L54)

**Context Token Handling**: Spatial omics data often includes auxiliary context tokens (modality, assay, specie) that are prepended to the actual gene expression tokens. Setting `without_context=True` excludes these auxiliary tokens from pooling by slicing `transformer_output[:, 3:, :]`, ensuring that predictions are based solely on the biological signal rather than technical metadata. This is particularly important for classification tasks where the biological content is the primary focus.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L157-L160), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L138-L144)

**Distributed Training**: The fine-tuning script supports distributed data parallel (DDP) training for handling large datasets. The DDP strategy is automatically adjusted based on whether the backbone is frozen (`"ddp"` for frozen, `"ddp_find_unused_parameters_true"` for unfrozen) to optimize memory usage and computational efficiency.

Sources: [_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/_fine_tune.py#L50-L52)

## Common Use Cases

**Tissue Region Classification**: Classify cells into anatomical regions or tissue compartments (e.g., cortical layers in brain, zones in liver). This uses `niche_classification` with `n_classes` equal to the number of regions. The model learns to associate spatial and molecular patterns with region-specific identities.

**Spatial Niche Identification**: Identify discrete spatial niches based on cellular neighborhood composition. Each niche represents a distinct microenvironment characterized by specific cell type distributions. This is ideal for understanding tissue organization and cellular interaction patterns.

**Cell Type Presence Prediction**: Use `niche_binary_classification` to predict which cell types are present in each cellular neighborhood. This provides a binary profile of cell type co-occurrence patterns, useful for understanding tissue heterogeneity.

**Multi-Label Marker Expression**: Apply `niche_multiclass_classification` to predict expression levels or states of multiple markers simultaneously. This captures complex biological states that cannot be represented by single categorical labels.

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L62-L82), [_config_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/config_files/_config_fine_tune.py#L1-L21)

## Troubleshooting and Best Practices

**Poor Classification Performance**: If accuracy is low, consider: (1) Reducing `lr` to `1e-5` or lower, (2) Unfreezing more layers with `freeze=False`, (3) Extracting features from multiple layers with `extract_layers=[8, 10, 11]`, (4) Enabling the extractor MLP with `extractor=True`, (5) Increasing training epochs or adjusting warmup duration.

**Overfitting**: Signs of overfitting include large gaps between training and validation accuracy. Mitigate by: (1) Freezing the backbone with `freeze=True`, (2) Using stronger regularization (increase gradient clipping, add dropout), (3) Reducing model capacity (fewer extract_layers), (4) Increasing batch size for more stable gradients.

**Class Imbalance**: When classes are highly imbalanced, use `ignore_zeros=True` to exclude the majority class from loss computation, or implement weighted sampling in the DataLoader to balance class representation during training.

Sources: [_nicheformer_fine_tune.py](src/nicheformer/models/_nicheformer_fine_tune.py#L194-L196), [_fine_tune_model.py](src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L195-L197)

## Next Steps

After mastering classification tasks, explore related topics:
- **[Regression Tasks and Density Prediction](20-regression-tasks-and-density-prediction)** for continuous value prediction tasks
- **[Fine-Tuning Model Architecture](18-fine-tuning-model-architecture)** for deeper architectural insights
- **[Transfer Learning Across Tissues and Technologies](22-transfer-learning-across-tissues-and-technologies)** for cross-domain adaptation strategies
- **[Layer Extraction and Reinitialization Strategies](21-layer-extraction-and-reinitialization-strategies)** for advanced layer manipulation techniques


# Regression Tasks and Density Prediction



Regression tasks in Nicheformer enable the model to predict continuous numerical values from spatial transcriptomics data, with two primary applications: predicting niche composition distributions and predicting local cell density. These tasks leverage the pre-trained transformer backbone through supervised fine-tuning, adapting the learned representations for regression objectives rather than classification or masked token prediction.

## Regression Task Architecture

The regression framework in Nicheformer extends the pre-trained transformer with task-specific linear heads that map learned embeddings to continuous outputs. The architecture distinguishes between two regression modalities: niche composition regression predicts per-cell-type values, while density regression predicts a single scalar representing the number of surrounding cells.

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L15-L110)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Input Tokens] --> B[Token Embedding]
    B --> C[Positional Encoding]
    C --> D[Transformer Encoder<br/>Pre-trained Layers]
    D --> E{Extract Layers<br/>Strategy}
    E --> F[Layer Mean Pooling]
    E --> G[Layer Sum Pooling]
    E --> H[Layer Concatenation]
    F --> I[Hidden Representation<br/>batch × seq_len × dim]
    G --> I
    H --> I
    I --> J{Regression Task Type}
    J --> K[niche_regression<br/>Linear: dim → dim_prediction]
    J --> L[density_regression<br/>Linear: dim → 1]
    K --> M[MSE Loss]
    L --> M
    M --> N[Prediction Output]
    
    style K fill:#e1f5ff
    style L fill:#fff4e1
```

The regression head is instantiated based on the `supervised_task` parameter during model initialization. For niche regression tasks, the linear head maps the backbone's hidden dimensionality to a per-cell-type prediction vector, while density regression uses a single-output linear head for scalar predictions. The model supports optional distribution regression through softmax normalization before computing MSE loss.

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L62-L94)

### Task Types and Head Configuration

| Task Type | Linear Head Shape | Output Dimension | Loss Function | Use Case |
|-----------|------------------|------------------|---------------|----------|
| `niche_regression` | `(dim_model, dim_prediction)` | `batch × dim_prediction` | MSELoss | Predict per-cell-type abundance values |
| `density_regression` | `(dim_model, 1)` | `batch × 1` | MSELoss | Predict local cell count around target cell |

The `dim_prediction` parameter determines the output dimensionality for niche regression, typically set to the number of cell types or niche categories being predicted. For density regression, this parameter is irrelevant as the output is always a scalar.

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L28-L31), [_config_fine_tune.py](/src/nicheformer/config_files/_config_fine_tune.py#L13-L15)

## Fine-Tuning Pipeline for Regression Tasks

The regression fine-tuning workflow follows a structured pipeline that prepares data, configures the model, and trains with regression-specific loss computation. The training loop adapts the pre-trained backbone through supervised learning while optionally freezing layers or reinitializing specific transformer layers.

Sources: [downstream_fine_tune.py](/src/nicheformer/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.py#L17-L175)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Load AnnData] --> B[Load Technology Mean]
    B --> C[Create NicheformerDataset<br/>train/val/test splits]
    C --> D[Initialize DataLoaders]
    D --> E[Load Pre-trained Nicheformer]
    E --> F[Wrap in FineTuningModel<br/>Set supervised_task='regression']
    F --> G[Configure Trainer<br/>Gradient accumulation, checkpointing]
    G --> H[Train with MSE Loss]
    H --> I[Evaluate on Test Set]
    I --> J[Store Predictions in AnnData]
    
    style F fill:#ffe1f5
    style H fill:#e1ffe1
```

The dataset class handles metadata extraction including regression targets through the `metadata_fields` configuration. Targets are automatically converted to tensors and returned alongside the tokenized gene expression data during batch generation.

Sources: [dataset.py](/src/nicheformer/data/dataset.py#L139-L171)

### Configuration Parameters

Key configuration parameters control the regression fine-tuning behavior:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `supervised_task` | str | `'regression'` | Task type: `'niche_regression'` or `'density_regression'` |
| `regress_distribution` | bool | `False` | Apply softmax normalization to predictions |
| `predict_density` | bool | `False` | Sum label dimensions for scalar density prediction |
| `dim_prediction` | int | `1` | Output dimensionality for niche regression |
| `freeze` | bool | `False` | Freeze pre-trained backbone weights |
| `extract_layers` | List[int] | - | Which transformer layers to extract features from |
| `function_layers` | str | `'mean'` | How to combine extracted layers: `'mean'`, `'sum'`, `'concat'` |
| `extractor` | bool | `False` | Use pooler MLP head before linear prediction |

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L17-L39), [_config_fine_tune.py](/src/nicheformer/config_files/_config_fine_tune.py#L1-L21)

## Loss Computation and Training Dynamics

The regression training step computes Mean Squared Error between predictions and target labels, with special handling for density prediction tasks. When `predict_density=True`, the target labels are summed across dimensions to produce a scalar representing the total count of neighboring cells.

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L164-L203)

During the forward pass, the backbone generates hidden representations which are pooled using mean aggregation (excluding context tokens if `without_context=True`). The pooled representation passes through the regression linear head to generate predictions. For distribution regression, predictions undergo softmax normalization to ensure they sum to one across output dimensions.

The training loss is logged as `fine_tuning_regression_train` for monitoring convergence, while validation uses the corresponding `fine_tuning_regression_validation` metric.

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L107-L158), [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L216-L246)

### Density Prediction Mode

Density prediction extends the regression framework to predict local cellular microenvironment density. This mode is activated by setting `predict_density=True` in the model configuration, which triggers automatic label transformation:

```python
# Density prediction label transformation
if self.hparams.predict_density:
    label = batch['label'].sum(1)  # Sum across cell type dimensions
    label = label.view(-1, 1)      # Reshape to scalar prediction target
```

The density regression head maps the pooled representation to a single output value, trained to minimize MSE against the true neighbor count. This enables the model to learn spatial density patterns from gene expression context.

Sources: [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L183-L186), [_fine_tune_model.py](/src/nicheformer/models/_fine_tune_model.py#L89-L91)

## Prediction Extraction and Storage

After training, predictions are generated on the test set and stored back into the AnnData object for downstream analysis. The fine-tuning script handles both regression and classification task prediction extraction, with regression tasks returning the continuous predictions directly.

Sources: [downstream_fine_tune.py](/src/nicheformer/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.py#L145-L175)

Predictions are stored in `adata.obs` under a key formatted as `predictions_{label}`, where `{label}` is the target column name from the configuration. Test metrics computed during evaluation are stored in `adata.uns` with corresponding metric names for reference.

Sources: [downstream_fine_tune.py](/src/nicheformer/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.py#L156-L170)

> [!TIP]
> When using distribution regression with `regress_distribution=True`, ensure your target labels are properly normalized or comparable across samples, as the softmax normalization applied during prediction assumes comparable scales across output dimensions.

> [!TIP]
> For density prediction tasks, verify that your label dimensions represent additive quantities (such as neighbor counts) before enabling `predict_density=True`, as the summation operation assumes meaningful additive semantics across the label dimensions.

## Practical Implementation Example

The following configuration demonstrates setting up a niche regression task to predict per-cell-type niche composition values:

```python
sweep_config = {
    'checkpoint_path': "/path/to/pretrained/nicheformer.ckpt",
    'supervised_task': 'niche_regression',  # Regression task
    'regress_distribution': False,          # No softmax normalization
    'predict_density': False,               # Predict full vector, not scalar
    'dim_prediction': 33,                    # Predict 33 cell type values
    'freeze': False,                         # Allow backbone fine-tuning
    'extract_layers': [6, 7, 8],            # Extract last 3 layers
    'function_layers': 'mean',              # Average layer representations
    'extractor': False,                      # No pooler MLP
    'lr': 1e-4,
    'warmup': 100,
    'max_epochs': 50000,
    'batch_size': 12,
    'label': 'X_niche_0',                   # Target column in adata.obs
    'data_path': '/path/to/data.h5ad',
    'technology_mean_path': '/path/to/mean.npy',
}
```

For density prediction, modify the configuration as:

```python
{
    'supervised_task': 'density_regression',
    'predict_density': True,                # Sum labels to scalar
    'dim_prediction': 1,                     # Single output (required but ignored)
    # ... other parameters same as above
}
```

Sources: [_config_fine_tune.py](/src/nicheformer/config_files/_config_fine_tune.py#L1-L21), [downstream_fine_tune.py](/src/nicheformer/experiments/downstream_fine_tune.py#L80-L102)
